intro: Wet rooms are one of the most practical and stylish bathroom upgrades you can make, but getting the installation right is where most problems start. Rochester homeowners increasingly want that clean, open shower space — whether it's replacing a dated avocado suite in an Edwardian semi or modernising a poky bathroom on a post-war estate. The challenge is that wet rooms demand genuinely skilled waterproofing work, precise floor gradients, and a plumber who understands how your property's structure affects every decision. Get it wrong and you're looking at water damage that creeps into joists and subfloors for months before you notice. Get it right and you have a bathroom that works beautifully for decades.
localContext: Rochester's housing stock throws up some real variety when it comes to wet room work. The Edwardian semis you'll find across much of the town — particularly around the St Margaret's and Watts Avenue areas — typically have suspended timber floors, which need careful assessment before any wet room work begins. A solid concrete subfloor makes gradient work more straightforward, but suspended timber requires a specialist waterproofing build-up to protect the structure beneath. Post-war estate properties often have more predictable layouts but can have limited bathroom footprints, meaning design has to work harder. Newer developments in and around Rochester generally have more bathroom space and solid floors, making installation more straightforward. There's also the water to consider: Rochester sits in a moderately hard water area, which means limescale will form on shower screens and fittings over time. Many wet room installers working here recommend specifying quality brass fittings and frameless glass rather than cheap alternatives that deteriorate quickly in these conditions.
serviceDetail: A proper wet room installation in Rochester typically unfolds over five to seven working days, depending on the size of the space and any structural complications. The first stage is stripping out the existing bathroom completely and assessing the floor construction — this is when any issues with timber joists or damp in older Rochester properties usually come to light. If the floor needs strengthening or levelling, that's done before anything else. Next comes the tanking, which is the waterproof membrane system applied to the floor and all walls up to a minimum height. This is arguably the most important part of the entire job and where shortcuts lead to long-term damage. Once tanking is cured and tested, the floor is built up to create the correct fall towards the drain — typically around 1.5% gradient — so water flows away without pooling. Wall boards or tiles are then applied, with all joints and penetrations carefully sealed. Plumbing for the thermostatic shower valve, drain, and any additional fittings like a basin or WC comes next, followed by final tiling or wall finishing, fitting of shower controls, screen if specified, and full silicone detailing. A good installer will walk you through the finished job and explain how to maintain the silicone seals, which is especially relevant in Rochester's hard water conditions where limescale can undermine seal integrity over time if not cleaned regularly.
pricing: Wet room installation in Rochester typically runs between £6,000 and £12,000 for a full project. At the lower end of that range you're looking at a straightforward conversion in a property with a solid concrete floor, modest tiling, and a mid-range shower system. Costs climb towards the upper range when suspended timber floors need specialist treatment, the bathroom requires structural work, or you're specifying premium fittings, large-format tiles, or underfloor heating. Underfloor heating itself adds roughly £400 to £800 depending on floor area. In Rochester's older Edwardian properties, it's not unusual for unexpected damp or joist work to add £500 to £1,000 to the original quote, so always ensure your installer has properly surveyed the subfloor before pricing.
whyLocal: Choosing a tradesperson based in or around Rochester rather than a national firm makes a real difference on a project like this. Local installers know the property types here — they've worked in the Edwardian terraces, the post-war semis, and the newer builds, and they understand the quirks that come with each. They're also familiar with local building control requirements and can advise on whether your wet room project needs notification under Part L or Building Regulations. When something unexpected comes up mid-job, a local tradesperson can source materials quickly from nearby merchants rather than waiting on deliveries, keeping the project moving and your home liveable.

faqs.q: Do I need planning permission for a wet room installation in Rochester?
faqs.a: In most cases, no. Wet room installations are considered permitted development for internal bathroom work. However, if your Rochester property is listed — and there are several in and around the city centre — you'll need listed building consent before making any alterations. It's worth checking with Medway Council if you're unsure about your specific property's status.

faqs.q: Can a wet room be installed in an Edwardian semi with a timber floor?
faqs.a: Yes, but it needs to be done properly. Suspended timber floors require a specific waterproofing system — typically a combination of a rigid tile backer board and a tanking membrane rather than simply tiling over the existing floor. An experienced Rochester installer will assess the joist condition and spacing first, and may recommend some reinforcement before the wet room build-up begins.

faqs.q: How do I maintain a wet room in Rochester's hard water conditions?
faqs.a: Limescale is the main enemy of wet rooms in this part of Kent. Wiping down glass screens and tiles after each shower makes a significant difference, and using a squeegee takes less than a minute. A diluted white vinegar solution works well for regular descaling. Also inspect your silicone seals every six months — hard water and soap scum can degrade them faster than in softer water areas, and replacing silicone early is far cheaper than dealing with water ingress.

faqs.q: How long does a wet room installation take in Rochester?
faqs.a: Most wet room projects in Rochester take between five and seven working days. Simpler conversions in modern properties with solid floors can sometimes be completed in four days. Older Edwardian properties where additional floor or damp work is needed can stretch to eight or nine days. Your installer should give you a clear programme before work starts so you can plan around the bathroom being out of use.
